slides.title: The nurse in the emergency department (ED) is caring for a 9-year-old client wit
text:
Question: The nurse in the emergency department (ED) is caring for a 9-year-old client with asthma. Parent at bedside. Client reports chest tightness with cough especially at night for the past 2 evenings. Expiratory wheeze auscultated throughout the chest. Vital signs: T 98.6 °F (37°C), P 110, RR 28, pulse oximetry reading 89% on room air. Sitting in tripod position with arms draped over bedside table. Humidified supplemental oxygen applied at 2 L/min via nasal cannula.
Complete the following sentence by choosing from the list of options.
The nurse should first _____.
A. Ask parent about allergens in the home.
B. Check the client’s peak flow with a peak expiratory flow meter.
C. Administer albuterol to the client.
D. Remind the client how to use metered dose inhaler.
Correct answer: C. Administer albuterol to the client.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Administer albuterol to the client.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Administer albuterol to the client.” – Rapid bronchodilation relieves acute obstruction
Not correct:
• “Ask parent about allergens in the home.” – History can wait until acute symptoms treated
• “Check the client’s peak flow with a peak expiratory flow meter.” – Peak flow can follow rescue therapy when appropriate
• “Remind the client how to use metered dose inhaler.” – Teaching follows stabilization
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 26: “Beta2-adrenergic agonists (albuterol)”
• Unit 1 - NCLEX Test Taking Strategies, slide 19: “apply humidified supplemental oxygen at 2L/min via nasal cannula”

Your Unit 1 slide 19 uses this same scenario ("The nurse should first ...") with humidified oxygen as one of its options and no answer shown; oxygen is not offered in this quiz version, and your Respiratory slide lists albuterol as a quick-relief medication.

slides.title: The nurse uses a diagram to show that when the diaphragm moves
text: Question: The nurse uses a diagram to show that when the diaphragm moves
A. up, the decreased negative pressure allows air to enter the lungs.
B. down, the negative pressure in the thoracic space pulls air into the lungs.
C. up, the increased negative pressure in the thoracic space forces air into the lungs.
D. down, the intercostal muscles retract, forcing air out of the lungs.
Correct answer: B. down, the negative pressure in the thoracic space pulls air into the lungs.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• down, the negative pressure in the thoracic space pulls air into the lungs.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “down, the negative pressure in the thoracic space pulls air into the lungs.” – Downward contraction increases thoracic volume and draws air in
Not correct:
• “up, the decreased negative pressure allows air to enter the lungs.” – Upward motion reduces thoracic volume
• “up, the increased negative pressure in the thoracic space forces air into the lungs.” – Upward motion promotes expiration
• “down, the intercostal muscles retract, forcing air out of the lungs.” – Downward movement promotes inspiration
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client with the following ABG result. pH 7.49 PaCO2 41
text:
Question: The nurse is caring for a client with the following ABG result.
pH 7.49
PaCO2 41mmHg
HCO3 38mEq/L
Which of the following is an appropriate interpretation of these results?
A. metabolic acidosis
B. respiratory alkalosis
C. Metabolic alkalosis
D. respiratory acidosis
Correct answer: C. Metabolic alkalosis
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Metabolic alkalosis
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Metabolic alkalosis” – High pH and high bicarbonate
Not correct:
• “metabolic acidosis” – pH is elevated, not low
• “respiratory alkalosis” – CO2 is not low
• “respiratory acidosis” – CO2 is not elevated
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 2 - Reduction of Risk Potential, slide 30: “pH greater than 7.4 = Alkalinity”
• Unit 2 - Reduction of Risk Potential, slide 30: “HCO3: 22-28 mEq/L (Metabolic)”
Worked out with the normal ranges on your slide: high pH with normal CO2 and high HCO3 is metabolic alkalosis.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for an adult client who has an ABG return with the following
text:
Question: The nurse is caring for an adult client who has an ABG return with the following values:
pH 7.30
CO2 49
HCO-3 23
K+ 4.9
Based on the ABG, which of the following interventions is appropriate?
A. Position the client in a low-Fowlers position.
B. Encourage the client to use the incentive spirometer.
C. Have the client breath into a paper bag.
D. Inform the client to slow their respirations down.
Correct answer: B. Encourage the client to use the incentive spirometer.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Encourage the client to use the incentive spirometer.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Encourage the client to use the incentive spirometer.” – Promotes lung expansion and ventilation
Not correct:
• “Position the client in a low-Fowlers position.” – Low position limits lung expansion
• “Have the client breath into a paper bag.” – Unsafe without confirming cause of hyperventilation
• “Inform the client to slow their respirations down.” – May worsen hypoventilation
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 2 - Reduction of Risk Potential, slide 30: “PacCO2: 35-45mm Hg (Respiratory)”
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 4: “Encourage client to turn, cough, and deep breath, splint chest wall, use incentive spirometer”
Worked out with the ranges on your slide: low pH with high CO2 is respiratory acidosis; incentive spirometry is on your pneumonia slide.

slides.title: The nurse is assessing voice sounds during a respiratory assessment. Which of th
text: Question: The nurse is assessing voice sounds during a respiratory assessment. Which of these findings indicates a normal assessment? (Select all that apply).
A. When the patient speaks in a normal voice, the examiner can hear a sound but cannot exactly distinguish what is being said.
B. As the patient repeatedly says “ninety-nine,” the examiner clearly hears the words “ninety-nine.”
C. Voice sounds are faint, muffled, and almost inaudible when the patient whispers “one, two, three” in a very soft voice.
D. As the patient says a long “ee-ee-ee” sound, the examiner hears a long “aaaaaa” sound.
E. As the patient says a long “ee-ee-ee” sound, the examiner also hears a long “ee-ee-ee” sound.

Correct answers: A. When the patient speaks in a normal voice, the examiner can hear a sound but cannot exactly distinguish what is being said.; C. Voice sounds are faint, muffled, and almost inaudible when the patient whispers “one, two, three” in a very soft voice.; E. As the patient says a long “ee-ee-ee” sound, the examiner also hears a long “ee-ee-ee” sound.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• When the patient speaks in a normal voice, the examiner can hear a sound but cannot exactly distinguish what is being said.
• Voice sounds are faint, muffled, and almost inaudible when the patient whispers “one, two, three” in a very soft voice.
• As the patient says a long “ee-ee-ee” sound, the examiner also hears a long “ee-ee-ee” sound.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “When the patient speaks in a normal voice, the examiner can hear a sound but cannot exa…” – Normal speech is muffled
• “Voice sounds are faint, muffled, and almost inaudible when the patient whispers “one, t…” – Whispered sounds are normally faint
• “As the patient says a long “ee-ee-ee” sound, the examiner also hears a long “ee-ee-ee” …” – Normal E sound remains E
Not correct:
• “As the patient repeatedly says “ninety-nine,” the examiner clearly hears the words “nin…” – Clearly transmitted words suggest bronchophony
• “As the patient says a long “ee-ee-ee” sound, the examiner hears a long “aaaaaa” sound.” – E-to-A change is egophony
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:

• There is a decrease in symptoms of tuberculosis along with improved chest x-rays and sputum cultures.
